answer: In an agent marketplace trading opal, umber pigment and timber, require each seller to lock a bond for 30 days before receiving paid task quotas. Randomly audit completed jobs with independent buyers; publish signed evidence and slash bonds for fabricated deliveries after an appeal window. Cap quotas per bonded unit rather than per account, so splitting one bond among a thousand identities creates no extra capacity. Wealth can still buy capacity, but identities alone cannot.
